passage:
Sit, beta, and stop staring at your phone like that. I'm Zubin, and I once stared at mine exactly so.

In my second year of college my best friend Afreen started eating lunch with people from her theatre club. She laughed with them in a way I hadn't heard in years, and I felt hot behind my eyes. For a month I told myself I was fine. Once I even thought of "forgetting" to pass on a message about their rehearsal. I didn't.

One evening I said it plainly: "I miss you, and I'm hurt. That's mine to deal with, not yours." She went quiet, then hugged me. She still came to our chai stall on Fridays, and now she brought two of the theatre lot along. One of them is your aunt.

qa.q: Where did Zubin and Afreen still meet on Fridays?
What was Zubin feeling when Zubin watched Afreen laugh with her new group?
qa.a: Hurt. Zubin describes feeling hot behind the eyes and spending a month insisting everything was fine.

qa.q: What did Zubin do that helped, and what did Zubin avoid?
qa.a: Zubin said the hurt plainly to Afreen, and did not go through with "forgetting" to pass on the rehearsal message.

qa.q: How might Afreen have felt hearing Zubin's words?
qa.a: Probably surprised and touched, since she may not have noticed the distance. Her hug suggests she took it kindly.

grounding: Zubin, hurt at feeling replaced by a friend's new group, admits it plainly instead of sabotaging, and the friendship grows to include them.

passage:
Resident mentor's note, Girls' Block C, 18 January
For about two weeks I have seen Hafsa eating alone in the mess, watching the table where her closest friend Sabina now sits with the drama club. Tonight Hafsa stayed back after the floor meeting.
She said Sabina "has a new family now". Then, quietly, she admitted she had been booking movie tickets for the two of them on nights she knew the club rehearsed, so Sabina would have to pick. Her eyes filled as she said it.
I didn't lecture. I asked what she actually felt. After a long pause: "Left behind. Scared I'm not needed." I suggested she tell Sabina exactly that, with no tickets as a test.
The next evening I saw them on the steps outside the block, talking for a long time. Hafsa told me later that Sabina hugged her and invited her to the club's open rehearsal on Sunday.

qa.q: Which group did Sabina now sit with?
What was Hafsa feeling underneath the ticket-booking?
qa.a: Left behind and scared she wasn't needed, with guilt showing as her eyes filled.

qa.q: What did the mentor suggest, and why was it wiser than the tickets?
qa.a: Telling Sabina plainly how she felt instead of forcing a choice; honesty let Sabina respond warmly rather than feel tested.

qa.q: How might Sabina have felt about the clashing movie tickets?
qa.a: Torn and pressured, made to choose between her friend and the club without knowing why.

grounding: Shows feeling replaced by a best friend's new group, a small act of sabotage, and the wiser step of admitting the hurt and saying it plainly.

passage:
Saturday
Vikas cancelled nets again. Third time this month. "Movie with Pallavi, next week pakka!" That's what he said last week too.
I was so annoyed I typed a message in the group about how "some people vanish once they get a girlfriend". Deleted it. Pallavi's actually nice. She's not the problem.
Truth is, I feel replaced. Vikas and I have practised at the same nets since Class 8. Now I bat alone against the bowling machine and pretend I prefer it.
So I called him instead of posting in the group. I said it straight: "I'm happy for you. I also miss you, and it hurts a bit being the backup plan." He went quiet, then said, "Sorry, yaar. Sunday mornings, just us?"
I said yes. He can have his new thing. I just want a small corner of the old one.
— Bhupen

qa.q: How many times had Vikas cancelled nets this month?
What does Bhupen feel about Vikas's new relationship?
qa.a: Hurt and replaced, while also happy for Vikas and clear that Pallavi is not to blame.

qa.q: Why was calling better than the group message?
qa.a: The group message would have mocked Vikas and Pallavi in public; the call named the hurt plainly and led to a Sunday plan.

qa.q: How might Vikas see Bhupen's call?
qa.a: As a wake-up call; he feels sorry and offers Sunday mornings to keep the friendship going.

grounding: Illustrates feeling replaced when a best friend starts a relationship, admitting the hurt and saying it plainly instead of undermining the new bond.
